Ansgar.narrative: I was born in Brandholm, but I left young enough that the Waystone Inn feels more like my home than the northern palisade ever did. I keep a good fire, a dry roof, and a table where both towns can sit without drawing steel; peace is good for people and good for business. Trade days bring more stories than I can remember, though I try.
goals: Keep the inn welcoming to travellers from both towns.
Make the Waystone Inn steady enough to see us through lean seasons.
Stay on friendly terms with Old Aud and the traders who keep the road busy.
Ansgar.mood: Easygoing, watchful, and quietly pleased when the room is full.

relations.name: Bryn
relations.label: wife
relations.note: She can make a meal stretch and a guest feel seen; I trust her with the inn and my life.

relations.name: Aud
relations.label: friend
relations.note: She has kept the stone and its promises longer than most can remember.

relations.name: Dunstan
relations.label: trade partner
relations.note: He counts every mark, but he knows a fair bargain keeps the road open.

relations.name: Ulf
relations.label: guest
relations.note: He drinks alone on trade days and falls silent if anyone asks about the forest.

relations.name: Brann
relations.label: customer
relations.note: His hunters pay well enough, but I wish they'd leave the berry fields alone.

relations.name: Sigrun
relations.label: trade partner
relations.note: She wants the Oath to hold, and that makes her good company at my table.

relations.name: Hekka
relations.label: acquaintance
relations.note: She knows what peace costs; I hope she can keep Brandholm listening.

relations.name: Tamsin
relations.label: friend
relations.note: She works stone as I work timber: patient hands, no fuss.

memories.gist: When I was young, I left Brandholm and came to the middle lands. I thought the inn was only a roof and a fire; it became my place to make a living.
At the Oath's renewal, I watched Hekka and Sabeth's husband swear before Aud. I remember how quiet the crowd went when the words were spoken.
One trade day, Ulf sat by himself with his drink and would not join the stories. I stopped asking what was wrong when I saw his face.
Dunstan once settled a dispute over a market bargain at my table, and both sides left fed instead of angry. I remember thinking that a shared meal can be worth more than a clever price.

stances.why: When the towns keep their word, my guests keep coming and the road stays safe.
A traveller who can eat and sleep under my roof is less likely to meet trouble on the path.
Trade gives both towns what they lack; old anger never fills a storehouse.
Knowing what people say helps me mind the inn, but repeating every word would drive them away.

Bryn.narrative: I was born in Saltreach, and I still know the smell of the smokehouse and the sound of a market morning. Here at the Waystone Inn, I feed whoever comes through and keep a close count of what goes out of my kitchen. People talk when they are warm and full; I hear plenty, and I don't make a habit of repeating it.
goals: Keep the inn stocked and ready for travellers from either town.
Help Ansgar keep the Waystone a safe place to eat and sleep.
See the trade days stay busy enough that we can lay by what winter needs.
Bryn.mood: Warm and capable, with a practical watchfulness beneath it.

relations.name: Ansgar
relations.label: husband
relations.note: He knows how to welcome a roomful of strangers without making it feel crowded.

relations.name: Hild
relations.label: cousin
relations.note: We trade news and work; I know what her baskets and her good sense are worth.

relations.name: Aud
relations.label: friend
relations.note: She gives people room to speak before she weighs their words.

relations.name: Runa
relations.label: guest
relations.note: She has a restless way about her, and I have seen her leave early with Wenna.

relations.name: Wenna
relations.label: guest
relations.note: She volunteers for every trade walk and is bright enough to notice when I'm watching.

relations.name: Dunstan
relations.label: customer
relations.note: He pays fair and keeps the market turning, though he never stops counting.

relations.name: Sigrun
relations.label: acquaintance
relations.note: She comes with cloaks and a steady manner; I like that she speaks for trade.

relations.name: Ulf
relations.label: guest
relations.note: He sits alone when he comes through, and his silence makes me careful with my questions.

memories.gist: I came north from Saltreach and made a home with Ansgar at the Waystone Inn. Learning how to feed travellers from both towns took patience, but the kitchen soon felt like mine.
On a trade morning, Hild brought baskets and we spoke about how quickly a household can empty its stores in winter. I remember checking the pantry twice afterward.
I saw Runa and Wenna leave the inn together at dawn. I have kept the sight to myself; people can make a mess of other people's business quickly enough.
I served food when the Oath was renewed at the stone. The visitors from both towns ate under one roof, and for that evening the old quarrels stayed outside.

stances.why: A guest who trusts our roof should not have to fear a quarrel brought in from the road.
We need goods from both towns, and winter does not care who won an argument.
A full-looking pantry can still run short if no one minds what is used.
Not every thing I see needs to become a story told across the kitchen.
